follow-up time: 72 hours after delivery or after consumption of four bars, whichever was later
exposure: Mode of delivery (Caesarean section vs vaginal delivery)
outcome: time to first noticeable breast fullness
Global assessment of the satisfaction of mothers with lactation, the well-being of the child, taste, and ease of use
cohort: Women with gestational age 37 weeks or more who intended to breastfeed
finding: The study found that the use of the Shavari bar (containing Shatavari and oats) resulted in a higher mean total milk volume expressed and a shorter time to breast fullness compared to the placebo bar in postpartum women.
mod_finding: This study mentions cesarean section as a mode of delivery for some participants but does not examine its relationship to the primary outcome (breast milk output).
